Kawanthissa’s death: Minister rejects news report attributing cause to diarrhoea

cards.what_happened: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi denied saying that elephant Kawanthissa died from diarrhoea. He said a daily Sri Lankan Sinhala-language newspaper report was inaccurate. He stressed that only a post-mortem report can determine the real cause of death.
details: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi issued a statement today (23) denying that he said elephant Kawanthissa died from diarrhoea. He was responding to a report in a daily Sri Lankan Sinhala-language newspaper that claimed the elephant's death was due to diarrhoea.

The minister said he never made that statement and that no one can decide the cause of death based on personal opinion. He said the cause, whether diarrhoea, a gunshot injury, or another reason, must be found through scientific and medical examinations. The final determination will come from the post-mortem report.

He warned that attributing false statements to him could spread misinformation and create public misconceptions. He asked the newspaper to correct the inaccurate report and share his real position with the public. He said the correction should have the same prominence as the original report.
key_facts: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi denied saying Kawanthissa died of diarrhoea.
A daily Sri Lankan Sinhala newspaper reported the elephant died from diarrhoea.
The minister issued his denial today (23).
He said only a post-mortem report can determine the cause of death.
Possible causes include diarrhoea, gunshot injury, or another cause.
He warned false statements spread misinformation and public misconceptions.
He asked the newspaper to correct the report with equal prominence.
cards.blurb: Environment Minister denies saying elephant Kawanthissa died of diarrhoea and demands a newspaper correction.
cards.spoken: Hello and welcome. Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi has spoken out after a newspaper report claimed that the elephant Kawanthissa died because of diarrhoea. The minister says he never said that. In a statement issued today (23), he explained that the real cause of death can only be confirmed by a post-mortem report. He said it could be diarrhoea, a gunshot injury, or something else, but only scientific and medical tests will tell. He is worried that false quotes spread misinformation and confuse the public. So he has asked the newspaper to fix the story and share his actual position with the same importance as the original report. We will wait to see what the post-mortem examination reveals.

Two fishermen killed after being hit by train in Trincomalee

cards.what_happened: Two fishermen died and a third person was badly hurt after a train hit them in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd. The three were standing on the railway track when a train going from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort struck them. One died at the scene and another later died in hospital.
details: Police said three people were standing on the railway track when a train travelling from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort hit them in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd. One person died right at the spot.
The other two were taken to Trincomalee Hospital with serious injuries. One of them later died while being treated, bringing the death toll to two.
The two dead men were both fishermen, aged 48 and 58, from the Matara and Dondra areas. Their bodies were placed at the Trincomalee Hospital mortuary.
The China Bay Police are looking further into what happened.
key_facts: Two fishermen died and one person was seriously hurt after a train hit them.
It happened in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd.
The three were standing on the railway track when the train struck them.
The train was travelling from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort.
One person died at the scene; another died later in hospital.
The dead were fishermen aged 48 and 58 from Matara and Dondra.
Their bodies were placed at the Trincomalee Hospital mortuary.
China Bay Police are investigating further.
cards.whats_next: The China Bay Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.
cards.blurb: Two fishermen died and a third was badly hurt when a train struck them on a railway track in Trincomalee.
cards.spoken: Here's a sad story from Trincomalee. On the night of the twenty-second, three people were standing on a railway track near the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour when a train came through. Police say the train was heading from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort, and it struck all three of them. One person died right there at the scene. The other two were rushed to Trincomalee Hospital with serious injuries, but sadly one of them also died while being treated. The two who lost their lives were both fishermen, aged forty-eight and fifty-eight, and they came from the Matara and Dondra areas. Their bodies have been kept at the hospital mortuary. The China Bay Police are now investigating exactly how this happened.

location.place: Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area, Trincomalee
